brief: GS Credit MarketStrats (Biswas) notes EUR rates widened 5-10bps and USD rates 15-20bps last week, pushing both to 10-year highs; positioning was already defensively short going in, which skews near-term risk toward a relief rally absent an upside inflation surprise. Equities held up (SPX +1.2%, NDX +3.25%, SX5E +1%) on light positioning, supporting SPX calls given low implied vols. Credit widened broadly, with EUR Senior Financials cash and AT1/Corp Hybrids underperforming and bonds lagging iTraxx/CDX; deteriorating net issuance-minus-flows and negative total returns (via positive rates/spread correlation) argue for caution, but equity resilience, an expected October issuance slowdown, and improved valuations (many pockets above the 70th percentile on a 1-year lookback) argue against turning bearish yet. Preferred expressions: long GSLCIF5Y (Senior Fins), long GSLCEUHS (Hyperscalers), selling iTraxx Main October straddles for carry; hedge-minded investors can short EUR BB via GSLCH2B4, since BBs still screen rich (8th percentile, 10-year lookback) despite a HY-refinancing headwind. Separately, French 10y OAT-Bund spreads widened to above 110bps, now exceeding iTraxx SubFin for the first time ever, an outsized move the desk sees as an asymmetric short-SubFin/long-OAT-Bund trade.
